question.text: As per SEBI regulations, what is the cut-off time for purchase applications and switch-ins in equity and debt schemes, and how is the applicable NAV determined?

answer.text: 3:00 PM on a business day; for equity/debt purchases and switch-ins, the applicable NAV is that of the business day on which funds are available for utilisation before the cut-off, irrespective of the time of receipt of the application

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series V-A workbook (pp.190-192), the cut-off time for purchase applications and switch-ins in equity and debt schemes is 3:00 PM on a business day. The applicable NAV is the closing NAV of the business day on which the funds are available for utilisation before the cut-off, irrespective of the time of receipt of the application. The Trap: 1:30 PM is the cut-off for liquid/overnight purchases, not equity/debt. 2:00 PM and 12:00 Noon are not the prescribed cut-offs for any standard scheme category. Note that merely getting the application in before 3:00 PM does not, by itself, guarantee same-day NAV for equity/debt — funds-availability for utilisation is the controlling event. Note: Advise clients to submit applications well before 3:00 PM and use a payment mode that achieves same-day credit (RTGS/NEFT/local cheque). Outstation cheques or DDs may delay funds availability and push the applicable NAV to a later business day.
